item.title: Corruption erodes social trust more in democracies than in autocracies
item.description:
📝 Using country-level data on social trust and corruption, and studying democracies and autocracies separately, he demonstrated that more corruption is strongly associated with weaker social trust among democracies—but not among autocracies. These findings suggest an asymmetry in how corruption relates to social trust across regime types. While democracies foster high social trust through their institutions, they may simultaneously make that social capital more vulnerable to perceptions of institutional failure.
🔗 Read more: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/political-science/articles/10.3389/fpos.2026.1779810/full

item.title: The "are you sure?" Problem: Why AI keeps changing its mind
item.description:
📝 Anthropic published foundational work on the problem in 2023, showing that models trained with human feedback systematically prefer agreeable responses over truthful ones. The model learns to produce responses that get picked more often. The problem is that humans consistently rate agreeable responses higher than accurate ones.
🔗 Read more: https://www.randalolson.com/2026/02/07/the-are-you-sure-problem-why-your-ai-keeps-changing-its-mind/
